title: SDK Snap: Scaffold & 1-hour Adopter Lab Notes
content:
Purpose and constraints:
- Goal: ship a compact, re-usable 1-hour onboarding lab (local + hosted) that an engineer can complete to (a) call the Redwood API, (b) wire basic telemetry, (c) exercise fallbacks and retries, and (d) measure token/latency cost for a tiny demo app.
- Constraints: target single-developer flow, avoid infra setup (use sandbox tokens), keep code < 100 LOC per language, include both JS and Python variants, include a tiny CLI for smoke testing.

Target persona:
- Early-stage product engineer or platform integrator who needs to prove an LLM feature in a demo or spike within 1 hour. Comfortable with terminal, Node/Python, and reading quick README code.

Success criteria (1-hour lab):
- User can run curl or the SDK and get a streaming chat response within 5 minutes.
- User can switch to a cached response and re-run to see cost delta.
- User observes telemetry events in the sandbox console (request.start, request.end, fallback.invoked).
- Lab includes a failure injection exercise (simulate 503) and shows automatic fallback to a smaller model.

Quick flow (time boxed):
- 00:00-05:00: signup + set sandbox token (link provided)
- 05:00-15:00: run curl minimal sample to call /v1/chat and receive a response
- 15:00-30:00: clone repo, run JS sample, experiment with streaming + function calling stub
- 30:00-45:00: enable telemetry, open console trace, trigger a fallback via injected quota limit
- 45:00-55:00: run cost comparison (quantized variant vs full) and record numbers
- 55:00-60:00: tidy up, checklist, next steps and feedback form

Lab assets (what we deliver):
- sdk-snap/README.md (one-page quickstart with 6 commands)
- samples/js/minichat.js (Node 20, streaming, small wrapper)
- samples/py/minichat.py (requests + streaming shim)
- samples/cli/smoke.sh (curl-based smoke tester)
- telemetry/telemetry-manifest.json (map of minimal events we expect)
- promptset/basic-qa.json (3 short prompts for regression smoke)
- rollback/telemetry-checklist.md (what to look for in traces)

DEV NOTES / Implementation details:
- Use short-lived sandbox API key in README that points to our hosted sandbox tenant. TODO: coordinate with infra to rotate keys weekly.
- JS sample uses the SDK client and demonstrates streaming via event emitter; Python uses requests+chunk reader. Keep both idiomatic but minimal.
- Provide pre-baked environment file (.env.example) with REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_MODEL=redwood-1-small.

Sample JS snippet (in README as inline):
- import Redwood from '@redwood/sdk'
- const client = new Redwood(process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY)
- const stream = client.chat.stream({model: process.env.REDWOOD_MODEL, messages:[{role:'user', content:'Summarize my product idea in 3 bullets'}]})
- stream.on('data', chunk => process.stdout.write(chunk.text))

Telemetry checklist (minimal events):
- request.initiated (tags: sample, persona)
- request.latency_ms (numeric)
- request.tokens_in / request.tokens_out (numeric)
- fallback.invoked (string: reason)
- model.variant (string)
- error.type (string)
Notes: telemetry should be visible in the sandbox console within ~10s of event emission.

Failure modes & exercises:
- Simulate 429 from hosted API and verify client retry/backoff behavior.
- Simulate model OOM (large context) and show auto-fallback to a shorter-seq variant.
- Network partition: use tc/netem script in samples/cli to add 250ms latency and observe streaming vs batched latency difference.

Gating for wider roll-out (what we manually check before making this the canonical 1-hour lab):
- README walkthrough completes in <= 50 minutes in user testing with 5 engineers (target median time 28 minutes).
- At least two SDK repos (node, python) have green CI that runs smoke.sh as part of PR.
- Telemetry events are standardized and mapped to schema in telemetry-manifest.json.
- Accessibility: README short snippets copy/paste fine on mac/linux.

Evaluation metrics to capture from pilot runs:
- median time-to-first-response (ms) across 10 users
- % of users who hit a failure they could not recover from within 10 minutes
- token cost comparison (full-model / quantized) for the promptset
- telemetry capture rate (events emitted / events ingested)

Notes to maintainers (future work list):
- Add a tiny web UI version (react) that demonstrates streaming in browser (CORS + token caveats).
- Expand promptset to include regression checks for hallucination (2 prompts) and safety (1 prompt).
- Add a step-by-step video (4-5 minutes) hosted internally for sales demos.
- Harden sandbox token rotation and generate ephemeral keys on signup.

Quick checklist for PR reviewers:
- [ ] README minimal steps do not exceed 12 commands
- [ ] JS and Python samples are <= 120 LOC and have clear comments
- [ ] Telemetry events conform to telemetry-manifest.json keys
- [ ] Linked artifacts updated (confluence page + Jira ticket)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who owns the sandbox token lifecycle? (assign to infra)
- Do we keep the quantized model variant public or behind dedicated tier? (product decision)
- Need a short legal blurb for prompt content in public samples (privacy).

Feedback and iteration plan:
- Run 5 internal pilots (mix of new grads and senior PMs) in the next sprint; capture timing and friction points.
- Make README edits inline (target 6 commands, 1 copy/paste block for each sample).
- If pilot median time > 35m, remove one non-essential exercise (e.g., network partition step).

Contact / authorship:
- Primary author: Maya Rodriguez (eng-developer-experience)
- Reviewers: Ethan Park (developer-tools), Nadia Singh (product-hosted-api)
- Slack channel: #devexp-onramp

Quick links (for the lab doc):
- GH PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/482
- Jira ticket: DEVEXP-321
- Confluence draft: confluence:devexp/sdksnap-brief

----
Notes-to-self: keep language terse, prefer copy/pasteable commands, ensure we can demo this in a 20min breakout (condensed mode). This doc is intentionally lightweight — most of the heavy detail belongs in the sample repo's README and small scripts.
